title: Writing good prompts
blurb: Simple ways to get more useful answers, first time.

slides.title: The model only knows what you tell it
body: A model can’t see your situation, your audience or what you’re aiming for. Leave those out and it fills the gaps with something generic.
A few extra sentences of detail usually make a bigger difference than anything else.

items.label: Vague prompt
items.text: Write an email about the hack day.

items.label: Specific prompt
items.text: Write a short, friendly email inviting 12 engineers to a hack day on Friday. Mention that lunch is provided and ask them to reply by Wednesday.

items.label: What changed
items.text: Audience, tone, length and the key details are all spelled out.

slides.title: What a good prompt usually includes
body: You don’t need all of these every time, but checking for them is a quick way to improve a prompt.
If you’d need to explain it to a new colleague, you probably need to explain it to the model.

visual.caption: A useful checklist, not a strict formula.

items.heading: Goal
items.text: What you want, and what it’s for.

items.heading: Context
items.text: Background, audience and any source material to use.

items.heading: Format
items.text: Length, structure and tone — bullets, a table, a two-line summary.

items.heading: Examples
items.text: One or two samples of what good looks like.

slides.title: Show, don’t just tell
body: Describing a style precisely is hard. Showing an example is easy, and the model is very good at following the pattern.
This works for tone, formatting, level of detail — almost anything you can demonstrate.

visual.caption: One example is often enough for the model to pick up the pattern.

items.label: Instruction
items.text: Rewrite each word in plain English, like the example.

slides.title: Treat it as a conversation
body: The first answer is a draft. Tell the model what to change, the same way you’d give feedback to a person.
And if a long chat has wandered off course, a fresh start with a better prompt often beats more corrections.

visual.caption: Good habits for any AI chat tool.

items.heading: Let it ask you
items.text: “Ask me any questions you need before you start.”

items.heading: Start fresh when stuck
items.text: A clean context window stops old mistakes carrying over.

quiz.question: Which prompt is most likely to get a useful answer?
options: Write a 100-word update for customers about our new search feature, in a friendly tone
quiz.explanation: It gives the goal, audience, length, topic and tone, so the model doesn’t have to guess.

quiz.question: Why does including an example in your prompt help?
options: It makes the prompt longer, which always helps
It shows the exact style or format, which is easier to match than a description
It gives the model new training
quiz.explanation: Examples demonstrate what you want directly. The model is good at continuing patterns it can see.

quiz.question: The first answer is close, but too long. What’s the best next step?
options: Give up and write it yourself
Ask the exact same question again
Ask it to shorten the answer, saying roughly how long
quiz.explanation: Specific feedback on the draft is usually the fastest route to the answer you want.
